title: The Seed the Scan Could Not Name — Adult Occult Sapodilla Seed Aspiration (Nguyen Phan 2026), Two-Year Unilateral Wheeze & Flexible Bronchoscopy Extraction (H049)

teenKit.tldr: A 55-year-old patient suffered through two years of misdiagnosed asthma and pneumonia before doctors discovered a tropical sapodilla fruit seed wedged deep inside her right lung, disguised by angry scar tissue. This case exposes how organic objects evade standard scans and why persistent symptoms demand a deeper look.
teenKit.whyItMatters: It proves that when standard medical treatments fail repeatedly, the body is often trying to tell us that we are treating the wrong problem entirely.
keyTakeaways: Organic foreign objects like seeds can hide in airways for years, mimicking common respiratory conditions like asthma and chronic pneumonia.
Medical imaging tools act like different detectives; some objects are radiolucent, meaning they don't show up easily on standard scans because of their material makeup.
When a foreign body stays in the lung too long, the body reacts by growing angry layers of granulation tissue around it, which can easily trick doctors into thinking it is a tumor.

vocab.meaning: The accidental breathing in of a foreign object, food, or liquid down into the windpipe and lungs.
Describing an object that X-rays and scans pass right through easily, making it extremely difficult to spot on imaging.
Fleshy, inflamed scar tissue that the body quickly builds up to heal an injury or wall off a foreign invader.
A medical procedure where a thin, lighted tube with a camera is snaked down the throat to inspect and clear the airways.

quiz.question: What condition was the 55-year-old patient incorrectly treated for over the course of two years?
quiz.explanation: Doctors repeatedly pumped her full of steroids and antibiotics for asthma and pneumonia because the trapped seed caused wheezing and recurring infections.

quiz.question: Why did the sapodilla seed manage to hide inside her lung for over 700 days without being immediately spotted?
options: It dissolved into liquid and reformed every night
It was invisible to the naked eye of the surgeon
It was radiolucent and masked by surrounding inflammatory scar tissue
It continuously migrated to different parts of her body
quiz.explanation: Organic material like a fruit seed doesn't light up easily on scans, and the body's own scar tissue grew over it to disguise it as normal tissue.

quiz.question: What happens when the body realizes a foreign object like a seed is stuck in the delicate airways of the lung?
options: It absorbs the object safely into the bloodstream
It instantly coughs it out completely
It attacks and dissolves the object with special enzymes
It builds up inflamed granulation tissue around it like a trap
quiz.explanation: The immune system reacts to the foreign intruder by growing angry layers of scar tissue around it, which can create tumor-like masses.
